### Observed differences

- Five activities that appear in none of the 200 earlier traces — A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — each occur in about 17–23% of later traces (roughly 33–45 of 200), at most once per trace; observed pairs of them never share a trace, and their combined share covers essentially every later trace (about 995 in 1000). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012, LAG002]

- Earlier, all observed outgoing transitions of A24 went to A25 and all of A25 went to A26. In the later window, about 52 in 100 of A24's outgoing transitions go to one of the five new activities (about 49 in 100 still to A25), and about 48 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions go to a new activity (about 52 in 100 still to A26). [DIR006, DIR007]

- The new activities execute between A24 and A26: in every trace where one co-occurs with A24 it comes after A24, and in every trace where it co-occurs with A26 it comes before A26 (shown directly for A14, A15 and A20, each co-occurring with both in about 21–23% of traces); each new activity is followed by A25 in roughly half of its outgoing transitions and by A26 in roughly the other half, and it occurs around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.5). [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

- Event distances shifted by one step: A24→A25, previously at distance 1 in all traces, is now at distance 1 in about 49 and distance 2 in about 52 of 100 traces; A25→A26 moved from all at distance 1 to about 52/48 at distances 1/2; and A24→A26 moved from distance 2 in all earlier traces to distance 3 in 199 of 200 later traces — exactly one inserted event per case. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A10 and A11 halved: mean about 1.0 hour earlier versus about 0.5 hour later (median 1.01 vs 0.51 hours; the middle 50% narrowed from roughly 0.87–1.13 hours to 0.45–0.56 hours), on similar numbers of observations (319 vs 336). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which, in the later window, virtually every case executes exactly one of five mutually exclusive alternative activities — A14, A15, A20, A21 or A22 — between A24 and A26, where earlier cases ran directly A24 → A25 → A26; the position of this step varies case by case, directly after A24 in about half the cases and directly after A25 in about half. The pattern is shown directly and consistently: the five activities are absent from all 200 earlier traces yet present in about 17–23% of later traces each, never co-occur and never repeat; A24 and A25 now route about half of their outgoing transitions to them; A24 always precedes and the new activity always precedes A26; and the A24→A26 distance grows from 2 to 3 in 199 of 200 later traces, indicating exactly one such step per case. With 34 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.44 expected for an unchanged process, this pattern as a whole cannot be explained by sampling variation. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, DIR007, REL004, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL015, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the evidence shows only participation, order and event distances, so it cannot establish whether these five activities are genuinely new work or a finer-grained recording of a step that existed earlier under other codes; zero participation in the earlier window means only that they were not observed there, and the outgoing profiles of the individual new activities rest on only about 33–45 traces each. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

Other differences: the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A10 and A11 halved, from a mean of about 1.0 hour in the earlier window to about 0.5 hour in the later one (median 1.01 to 0.51 hours, with a correspondingly narrower spread), on similar observation counts (319 vs 336); the time family produced 1 qualifying item against about 0.009 expected without a change, so this is a distinct, well-supported timing change in its own right, and the evidence cannot establish whether it is connected to the structural change above. [TWAIT001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 108 units tested, 0.45 items expected without change overall. By family:
- control_flow: 89 units tested, 34 items, 0.44 expected without change
- time: 19 units tested, 1 item, 0.009 expected without change

Control flow: 34 items vs 0.44 expected — that's ~77x the chance expectation. This is a massive count, far beyond chance. Time: 1 item vs 0.009 expected — that's ~111x the expectation. Both families have counts many times larger than expected by chance. So the screening comparison does not lead to "insufficient evidence" — the counts are many times larger than the chance expectation.

Now let's understand the behavioural story.

OCC items: A14, A15, A20, A21, A22 all had zero participation in the before window (0 occurrences per trace, 0% participation) and in the after window have participation of about 16.5%–22.5% (A14: 22.5%, A15: 21%, A20: 22%, A21: 16.5%, A22: 17.5%). Recurrence support 0 in both — so each appears at most once per trace. Support: before 0 traces, after 33–45 traces.

DIR items for A14, A15, A20, A21, A22: before profile empty (activity never observed), after profile shows outgoing transitions split roughly evenly between A25 and A26 (e.g., A14: 47% to A26, 53% to A25). So these new activities are followed by either A25 or A26, roughly 50/50.

DIR006 (A24): before, A24 always went to A25 (100%). After, A24 goes to A25 only 48.5%, with the rest redistributed to A14 (12%), A20 (11.5%), A21 (10%), A15 (9.5%), A22 (8.5%). So about half of A24's outgoing transitions now go to the new activities instead of directly to A25.

DIR007 (A25): before, A25 always went to A26 (100%). After, A25 goes to A26 52%, with the rest to A14 (10.5%), A15 (11.5%), A20 (10.5%), A22 (9%), A21 (6.5%). So about half of A25's outgoing transitions now go to the new activities instead of directly to A26.

POS items: A14, A15, A20, A21 appear at around position 0.5 of the trace (mean ~0.5, i.e., middle of the trace) in the after window; not observed before.

REL items:
- REL001 (A14, A15): before, neither present in any trace (100% neither). After: A_only 22.5%, B_only 21%, neither 56.5%, cooccurrence 0. So A14 and A15 never occur together; they occur in separate traces — alternatives.
- REL002 (A14, A20): similar — after: A_only 22.5%, B_only 22%, neither 55.5%, cooccurrence 0.
- REL003 (A14, A21): after: A_only 22.5%, B_only 16.5%, neither 61%, cooccurrence 0.
- REL007 (A15, A20): after: A_only 21%, B_only 22%, neither 57%, cooccurrence 0.
- REL008 (A15, A21): after: A_only 21%, B_only 16.5%, neither 62.5%, cooccurrence 0.
- REL012 (A20, A21): after: A_only 22%, B_only 16.5%, neither 61.5%, cooccurrence 0.

So A14, A15, A20, A21, A22 are mutually exclusive — never co-occur. They are alternatives.

- REL004 (A14, A24): before, A24 always present without A14 (B_only 100%). After: cooccurrence 22.5%, B_only 77.5%, and when they co-occur, order is B_before_A (A24 before A14) 22.5%. So A14 always comes after A24.
- REL005 (A14, A25): before, A25 always present without A14. After: cooccurrence 22.5%, B_only 77.5%; order mixed: A_before_B 12%, B_before_A 10.5%. Hmm, interesting — A14 and A25 co-occur in 22.5% of traces, with both orders in similar proportions (12% vs 10.5%). Wait, but DIR001 says A14 goes to A25 in 53% of its outgoing transitions. Hmm, but REL005 says when A14 and A25 co-occur, both orders appear. Actually wait — A14 → A25 as a direct successor would mean A14 before A25. But REL005 shows A_before_B 12% and B_before_A 10.5%. Hmm, that's odd. Actually, wait — maybe A25 also goes to A14 (DIR007 shows A25 → A14 10.5%). So in some traces A25 comes before A14 (A25 → A14 edge), and in others A14 comes before A25 (A14 → A25 edge). Hmm, but the co-occurrence is 22.5% and A_before_B + B_before_A = 22.5%, so whenever they co-occur there's a definite order.

Hmm wait, let me reconsider. Actually the REL components: cooccurrence 0.225 means both present in 22.5% of traces. A_before_B 0.12, B_before_A 0.105 — these sum to 0.225, so all co-occurrences have a fixed order within the trace (no interleaving). Both orders appear in similar proportions.

Hmm, but DIR001 says A14's outgoing transitions: A25 53%, A26 47%. And DIR007 says A25's outgoing: A26 52%, A14 10.5%, A15 11.5%, A20 10.5%, A22 9%, A21 6.5%. So A25 → A14 exists too. So the structure is more complex.

- REL006 (A14, A26): before, A26 always present without A14. After: cooccurrence 22.5%, B_only 77.5%, A_before_B 22.5%. So whenever A14 and A26 co-occur, A14 is always before A26. So A14 → ... → A26 always.

- REL009 (A15, A24): after: cooccurrence 21%, B_before_A 21% (A24 before A15).
- REL010 (A15, A25): after: cooccurrence 21%, A_before_B 9.5%, B_before_A 11.5% (mixed).
- REL011 (A15, A26): after: cooccurrence 21%, A_before_B 21% (A15 always before A26).
- REL013 (A20, A24): after: cooccurrence 22%, B_before_A 22% (A24 before A20).
- REL014 (A20, A25): after: cooccurrence 22%, A_before_B 11.5%, B_before_A 10.5% (mixed).
- REL015 (A20, A26): after: cooccurrence 22%, A_before_B 22% (A20 always before A26).

LAG items:
- LAG001 (A24, A25): before, the pair A24→A25 within 5 steps always at lag 1 (100%). After: lag 1 48.5%, lag 2 51.5%. So the direct A24→A25 adjacency is now at distance 2 in about half the cases — consistent with a new activity inserted between A24 and A25 in about half the traces.
- LAG002 (A24, A26): before, A24→A26 at lag 2 always (100%). After: lag 3 99.5%. So the distance from A24 to A26 increased from 2 to 3 — one step inserted.
- LAG003 (A25, A26): before, A25→A26 at lag 1 always. After: lag 1 52%, lag 2 48%. So in about half the traces something is inserted between A25 and A26.

Counts 319 vs 336. So the time between A10 and A11 halved. Empirical strength 0.9995 with 2000 references. Time family: 1 item vs 0.009 expected — many times larger.

Now, what's the overall story? Let me reconstruct:

Before: A24 → A25 → A26 (a chain). A24 always to A25, A25 always to A26, A24 to A26 at lag 2, A24→A25 and A25→A26 at lag 1.

After: In about half of traces, between A24 and A25 (or A25 and A26) one of the new activities A14/A15/A20/A21/A22 is inserted. The new activities:
- Occur in ~17–22% of traces each, mutually exclusive (never co-occur), total ~ (22.5+21+22+16.5+17.5) = 99.5%... wait, that sums to about 99.5%? Let me add: 0.225+0.21+0.22+0.165+0.175 = 0.995. Wait, but "neither" in REL001 (A14, A15) is 56.5% — meaning in 56.5% of traces neither A14 nor A15 appears. That's consistent: A14 22.5% + A15 21% + neither 56.5% = 100%. And REL012 (A20, A21): 22% + 16.5% + 61.5% = 100%. So each pair of the new activities: both never co-occur, and "neither" is high because most traces contain one of the other three.

Sum of participations ≈ 99.5%, mutually exclusive → essentially every after-trace contains exactly one of {A14, A15, A20, A21, A22}. Hmm wait, but is that right? 0.225+0.21+0.22+0.165+0.175 = 0.995. Yes. So in the after window, virtually every trace includes exactly one of these five activities.

Hmm, but wait — DIR006 says A24 goes to A25 only 48.5% after, and to the new activities ~51.5% total (12+11.5+10+9.5+8.5 = 51.5%). And DIR007 says A25 goes to A26 52% and to new activities 48% (10.5+11.5+10.5+9+6.5 = 48%). So the new activities are inserted either between A24 and A25 (about half the traces) or between A25 and A26 (about half).

Check with LAG: LAG001 (A24→A25): lag 1 in 48.5% (direct, when no insertion between them), lag 2 in 51.5% (one activity inserted). LAG003 (A25→A26): lag 1 52%, lag 2 48%. LAG002 (A24→A26): lag 2 before, lag 3 after (99.5%) — always exactly one insertion somewhere between A24 and A26. 

So the picture: after, exactly one of the five new activities is inserted into the A24→A25→A26 chain in every trace — either between A24 and A25 (~half) or between A25 and A26 (~half). The five are mutually exclusive alternatives.

Wait, but REL005 (A14, A25) shows mixed order: A_before_B 12%, B_before_A 10.5%. If A14 were only inserted between A24 and A25, then A14 would always be before A25. But B_before_A 10.5% means A25 before A14 in some traces — consistent with A14 inserted between A25 and A26 in those traces (A25 → A14 → A26). And DIR007 shows A25 → A14 10.5%. And REL006 (A14, A26): A14 always before A26 (22.5%) — consistent: whether A14 is between A24 and A25 or between A25 and A26, it's always before A26. Similarly REL004 (A14, A24): A24 always before A14. So A14 sits strictly between A24 and A26 always. Same pattern for A15 (REL009: A24 before A15 always; REL011: A15 before A26 always) and A20 (REL013, REL015).

So the hypothesis: five new activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22) were introduced as mutually exclusive alternatives, each inserted exactly once per trace between A24 and A26 (either directly after A24, before A25, or after A25, before A26). Before, the path went directly A24 → A25 → A26.

Hmm, wait. Let me double check the "inserted between A24 and A25" vs "between A25 and A26" split. DIR006: A24 → new activities 51.5%, → A25 48.5%. DIR007: A25 → new activities 48%, → A26 52%. LAG001: A24→A25 lag 2 in 51.5%. LAG003: A25→A26 lag 2 in 48%. So roughly half the traces have the new activity between A24 and A25, half between A25 and A26.

Hmm, but actually wait. Let me reconsider: is it exactly one new activity per trace? Sum of participations 99.5% and mutual exclusivity (cooccurrence 0 for all pairs among the five: REL001, 002, 003, 007, 008, 012 all show cooccurrence 0). We don't have all 10 pairs, but 6 pairs shown all have cooccurrence 0. The sum being ~99.5% strongly suggests exactly one per trace. Also LAG002: A24→A26 lag 3 in 99.5% of traces — exactly one event between them (lag 3 means 2 events in between: A25 plus one new one). Actually lag 3 = A24, X, A25, A26 positions differ by 3, so 2 events in between. Before it was lag 2 (1 event in between: A25). So exactly one new event inserted between A24 and A26 in 99.5% of after-traces. That confirms: exactly one new activity per trace (in the after window), positioned between A24 and A26.

Wait, but hold on — LAG002 support is 200 before and 200 after, meaning the ordered pair (A24, A26) within five steps is observed in all 200 traces in both windows. Good.

Also note: the new activities' position is around 0.5 (middle of trace) per POS items — consistent with insertion in the middle of the A24→A25→A26 chain if the trace has ~6-7 events. Now the TWAIT item: A10 → A11 elapsed time halved from ~1.0h to ~0.5h. This is a separate timing change. The time family had 1 item vs 0.009 expected — far above chance. This is a hypothesis in its own right (a change in timing), per instructions: "A consistent change in these times is a hypothesis in its own right (a change in timing); it does not need a structural counterpart."

So we have two main differences:
1. Control flow: insertion of one of five new alternative activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22) between A24 and A26 in essentially every after-trace (previously direct A24 → A25 → A26). This is a structural change — activities added to the process.
2. Timing: the elapsed time between A10 and A11 completions halved (from ~1.0h to ~0.5h).

Now, how to judge support?

Screening comparison: control_flow 34 items vs 0.44 expected — many times larger (about 77×). Time: 1 item vs 0.009 expected — about 111×. Both far exceed chance. So we proceed to judge the hypothesis on directness, consistency, and ruling out competitors.

The structural hypothesis: "one of five new activities is inserted between A24 and A26 in each after-trace". Evidence:
- OCC: the five activities absent before, present in ~17–22% of traces after, mutually exclusive (REL cooccurrence 0), summing to ~100%.
- DIR: A24 previously always → A25; now ~half the transitions go to a new activity. A25 previously always → A26; now ~half go to a new activity.
- LAG: A24→A25 distance shifted from 1 to {1, 2}; A25→A26 from 1 to {1, 2}; A24→A26 from 2 to 3 (99.5%). This directly shows one insertion between A24 and A26 in nearly every trace.
- REL with A24/A26: A24 always before the new activity; the new activity always before A26. So the new activity sits between A24 and A26.
- POS: new activities at mid-trace positions.

This is direct, consistent, multi-indicator evidence. The insertion hypothesis is strongly supported. Is it "Supported hypothesis" level? The evidence directly shows: new activities appear (OCC), they sit between A24 and A26 (REL with A24 and A26, LAG), exactly one per trace (LAG002 lag 3 in 99.5%, mutual exclusivity, sum of shares ~100%). Competing explanations: could this be a rare variant appearing only in the after window? No — it's in ~100% of after traces and 0% of before traces, with 200 traces each. Could it be a shift in path frequencies? No — the activities were entirely absent before; this is addition of activities, not re-routing among existing paths. The guidance says: "It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window... these indicate that activities were added or removed, became optional or mandatory". So this is an addition of activities — a structural change.

One caveat: the DIR profiles for the new activities are based on 33–45 observations each (after only), which is moderate support. But the overall pattern is highly consistent.

Also note: the new activities' outgoing edges split ~50/50 between A25 and A26. So when inserted after A24 (before A25), the flow is A24 → X → A25 → A26; when inserted after A25, the flow is A24 → A25 → X → A26. Both orders between X and A25 appear (REL005, REL010, REL014 mixed orders) — for A14, A15, A20. We don't have REL for A21/A22 with A25, but DIR004/DIR005 show A21 and A22 also go to both A25 and A26.

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider whether the insertion point differs per activity or is random. For A14: DIR001 A14 → A25 53%, A26 47%. REL005 (A14, A25): co-occur 22.5%, A14 before A25 12%, A25 before A14 10.5%. So A14 is before A25 in 12% of traces and after A25 in 10.5%. So the insertion point varies per trace, not per activity. Fine — the hypothesis is "one of five alternatives inserted at a variable point between A24 and A26".

Actually, hmm, is it exactly "between A24 and A26"? REL004: A24 before A14 always (when co-occurring, 22.5%). REL006: A14 before A26 always. So yes, A14 strictly between A24 and A26. Same for A15, A20. Presumably A21, A22 too (no REL items for them with A24/A26 in the evidence, but DIR and LAG support the general pattern). Actually, we don't have OCC for A21/A22 with A24... we have OCC004 (A21), OCC005 (A22), DIR004 (A21 → A25/A26), DIR005 (A22 → A25/A26). And LAG002 shows exactly one event between A24 and A26 in 99.5% of traces. Since the five new activities are the only new participants and they're mutually exclusive, and each trace has exactly one event inserted, it follows each trace contains exactly one of the five (the sum ~99.5% confirms).

So the main hypothesis: a structural change — in the later window, every case passes through exactly one of five previously unobserved activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22), inserted between A24 and A26 (either between A24 and A25 or between A25 and A26, roughly half each); the five are mutually exclusive alternatives. Before, the flow went directly A24 → A25 → A26.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence is direct (OCC + DIR + REL + LAG all converge), consistent, and the screening count (34 vs 0.44 expected) is far beyond chance. Competing explanations: sampling of a rare variant is ruled out by the scale (0% → ~100% participation with 200 traces per window). What can't be fully ruled out... hmm. The evidence can't tell us why, but we shouldn't speculate about causes. Limitations: the exact insertion position varies (both between A24–A25 and A25–A26), and the DIR profiles of the new activities rest on 33–45 traces each; also we can't determine from positional data whether the new activities replace any timing... Actually a competing explanation: could the "insertion" actually be that the new activities were always there but... no, they had 0 participation before. Zero participation only means not observed — with 200 traces, an activity that appears in ~20% of traces would almost surely appear in 200 traces if it existed before at that rate. That's a reasonable statement.

Another competing explanation for the specific structure: maybe the new activities are not "inserted" but the whole segment A24→A25→A26 was replaced in some traces... but LAG002 shows A24→A26 within 5 steps in 99.5% of after traces at lag 3, and A24/A25/A26 all still occur in all traces (DIR006/DIR007 support 200/200; LAG support 200/200). The instructions say a timing change is a hypothesis in its own right and doesn't need a structural counterpart. Since we have a strong structural hypothesis, I'll make that the main hypothesis and report the timing change under "Other differences". Actually, hmm — which should be main? The structural one has far more evidence (34 items). The timing one is a single item but with empirical strength 0.9995 and a huge effect (halved). I'll keep structural as main, timing as other.

Wait — but should I consider "Supported hypothesis" for both? The support level is one line for the whole answer. The structural hypothesis is supported. The timing change is also strongly indicated (1 item vs 0.009 expected, strength 0.9995, consistent halving across all quantiles, ~320/336 observations). I'd say "Supported hypothesis" overall, with the main hypothesis being the structural insertion, and note the timing change as an additional supported difference under "Other differences".
